answer: The design leans on random re-execution by unrelated peers, released only after three unrelated confirmations, duplicates are caught by replay, not by name. The ember holds work receipts rather than names, so the velvet of a duplicated claim is visible before it can spread. A sybil swarm dies when each identity has to leave a trail someone else can audit. Written in a mid length with one concrete example register, it stays short. By the pigment of the epoch the only identities still standing are the ones whose work held up.
